The application initializes the dashboard by importing components from the central index.ts. 2. useLayoutPersistence hook loads layout configuration from localStorage and provides state management (load, save, migrate) to the parent component. 3. DashboardGrid consumes this layout state to render
coupling_risks: High coupling between DashboardGrid and useLayoutPersistence: The grid component likely depends on the specific shape of the state object returned by the hook, making schema changes risky.

Implicit dependency via index.ts: The index.ts file acts as a facade; if it re-exports specific internal types or if consumers import directly from index.ts without tree-shaking, changes in any component force re-evaluation of the whole module.

State Shape Coupling: PanelChrome and PanelPicker likely expect specific properties on the layout state (e.g., panel IDs, dimensions). If useLayoutPersistence changes the data structure, all UI components relying on it will break.
Local Storage Assumption: The entire unit assumes a browser environment with localStorage access; porting this logic to a server-side or non-browser environment requires significant refactoring.

The design is cohesive but tightly coupled to the specific data schema of the layout state; introducing a centralized LayoutContext or a Redux/Zustand store would decouple the persistence logic from the specific component tree, improving testability and reusability.
